questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Different climate, relative proximity to home country and a good educational system

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very nice stay

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, a Kuumi student were there to help with the apartment and was very good at answering questions

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a kuumi student from the host university who welcomed me, and helped me get settled

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: PSOAS had a lot of apartments for exchange students, so housing was not a problem

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was still very close to campus, and the other tenants studied at the university aswell, so all In all it worked out pretty well

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of help to get in to the registration process, it was pretty difficult to find out if the courses were online or onsite though..

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It all happened digitally, but a student coordinator was there to help

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student coordinator

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got in to all the classes, most of them turned out to be online, which for me was a downside, as I went abroad to experience another study culture on campus, which I feel like I missed when having to study from my apartment most of the time

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to ask whether or not the courses are online before even going there, for me, I ended up not being able to have more than two courses onsite in my study field

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level very fitting, some courses were a bit harder as the expectations of what you know about some topics are a bit different, but overall very fitting

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more online based

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Nature conservation: a geographic perspective, World regional geography, Physical Geography of Fennoscandia, Regional development and planning in northern Europe, Survival Finnish, Beginners' Finnish Course 1, Tourism, development and sustainability

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend the Finnish courses if your study plan allows it, very good way to meet other exchange students from all kinds of study fields, while some basic Finnish sentences will help a lot in getting to talk to the Finnish students

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing really

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Diary products were very cheap, other than that, the prices are very similar to Denmark. There is a huge focus on student discounts in Finland, so important to look out for that. Lunch at one of the ten restaurants on campus were for example only 2,7 euro as a student, instead of 9,80.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of initiatives for students! All the tickets for different parties or happenings can be bought from an app, an everybody is welcome, additionally, there were a lot of different sports everyday, that you could just register to for free, if you paid the unimove sports fee, which was pretty cheap

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed trying out a lot of different sports activities, like the Futsal, volleyball, fitness boxing and Ultimate frisbee.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The city itself doesn't have a lot, but going north by renting a car or by bus, is definitely worth some weekends

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy and similar to the danish one.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Events or sports works really well, but generally just not being shy of speaking to them. Everybody seem very friendly as soon as you got to chat with them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The general friendliness and openness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for a lack of sunlight, sign up for different events and activities in the beginning, and then figure out what you wanna do more of and what not. Make sure to call a student advisor, and discover if all the classes in your study field are online

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: not particularly

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: For me, the most rewarding thing, was probably the development of my everyday English, which I could feel get a lot better during my stay, but overall it was just all a great experience

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think the lack of sunlight took me by surprise, this comined with the fact that most of my study hours were spent online was a bit hard. Luckily there were all these sports classes and events that helped out a lot.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
